text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is usually a "silent killer" with no symptoms at all.
You can learn more about the condition through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: No feelings: You cannot typically feel when your blood pressure is high.
Years of damage: It can harm your heart, brain, and kidneys without any clues.
Testing required: Only a physical measurement with a cuff can confirm your levels.

text_blocks.snippet: When blood pressure rises to dangerous levels (above 180/120 mm Hg), rare and severe signs may happen:

You can read additional details on warning signs from the American Heart Association. If you have a reading above 180/120 mm Hg with chest pain, shortness of breath, or weakness, call 911 immediately.
